must_remember: A half-wave plate introduces a phase difference of $\pi$ or path difference of $\lambda/2$ between the ordinary (O-ray) and extraordinary (E-ray) components.
The thickness of a half-wave plate is given by $t = \frac{\lambda}{2|n_o - n_e|}$.

When linearly polarized light is incident on a half-wave plate at an angle $\theta$ to the optical axis, the emergent light remains linearly polarized but its plane of vibration is rotated by an angle $2\theta$.
In a negative uniaxial crystal like calcite, $n_e < n_o$, meaning the extraordinary ray travels faster than the ordinary ray.
In a positive uniaxial crystal like quartz, $n_e > n_o$, meaning the ordinary ray travels faster than the extraordinary ray.
A half-wave plate alters the handedness of circularly polarized light (e.g., right-handed becomes left-handed).

glossary.meaning: A polarized component of light inside a birefringent crystal that obeys ordinary laws of refraction and travels with velocity $v_o = c/n_o$.
A polarized component of light inside a birefringent crystal that does not obey ordinary laws of refraction and travels with velocity $v_e = c/n_e$.
The optical property of a material having a refractive index that depends on the polarization and propagation direction of light, characterized by $n_o$ and $n_e$.
An optical device made of a birefringent crystal cut parallel to the optical axis designed to introduce a $\pi$ phase shift between orthogonal polarization components.
A specific direction in a birefringent crystal along which the ordinary and extraordinary rays travel with the same velocity and experience no birefringence.
